es: Analizar un texto de opinión identificando su tesis, su tono y dos recursos de cautela o persuasión, y citar la frase que lo demuestra.

vocabulary.es: conceder un punto, admitir una razón

teaching.en: My thesis is that every cycling lane in the city centre should be physically separated from traffic, not merely painted on the road.
teaching.es: Mi tesis es que cada carril para bicicletas del centro debería estar separado físicamente del tráfico, y no solo pintado en la calzada.
teaching.explanationEs: La tesis es lo que el autor defiende y suele aparecer pronto: My thesis is… / I will argue that…
segments: My thesis is that every cycling lane in the city centre should
be physically separated from traffic, not merely painted on the road.
teaching.audioText: My thesis is that every cycling lane in the city centre should be physically separated from traffic, not merely painted on the road.

teaching.en: Protected routes may encourage hesitant families to cycle, but the writer presents that outcome as a likelihood rather than a promise, and she is right to hedge.
teaching.es: Las rutas protegidas pueden animar a familias dudosas a ir en bici, pero la autora presenta ese resultado como una probabilidad y no como una promesa, y hace bien en matizar.
teaching.explanationEs: May es un recurso de cautela: hedge es suavizar una afirmación que no puedes probar del todo.
segments: Protected routes may encourage hesitant families to cycle, but the writer presents that outcome
as a likelihood rather than a promise, and she is right to hedge.
teaching.audioText: Protected routes may encourage hesitant families to cycle, but the writer presents that outcome as a likelihood rather than a promise, and she is right to hedge.

teaching.en: Surely no sensible parent would send a child cycling beside heavy lorries? The writer treats the answer as obvious, and that is how a rhetorical question works.
teaching.es: ¿Acaso algún padre sensato mandaría a un niño en bici junto a camiones pesados? La autora da la respuesta por obvia, y así funciona una pregunta retórica.
teaching.explanationEs: Surely…? no espera respuesta: presenta la idea del autor como evidente y empuja al lector a estar de acuerdo.
segments: Surely no sensible parent would send a child cycling beside heavy lorries? The writer
treats the answer as obvious, and that is how a rhetorical question works.
teaching.audioText: Surely no sensible parent would send a child cycling beside heavy lorries? The writer treats the answer as obvious, and that is how a rhetorical question works.

teaching.en: Critics say that the scheme is too costly, so a fair writer will concede a point before she tries to make a case for the plan as a whole.
teaching.es: Los críticos dicen que el plan es demasiado costoso, así que un autor justo concederá un punto antes de intentar defender el plan en su conjunto.
teaching.explanationEs: Conceder un punto (concede a point) no debilita la tesis: al contrario, hace que el autor suene justo.
segments: Critics say that the scheme is too costly, so a fair writer will concede a
point before she tries to make a case for the plan as a whole.
teaching.audioText: Critics say that the scheme is too costly, so a fair writer will concede a point before she tries to make a case for the plan as a whole.

teaching.en: A sweeping statement such as everybody hates cycling may sound firm, but a single exception is enough to undermine it.
teaching.es: Una generalización excesiva como «todo el mundo odia ir en bici» puede sonar firme, pero basta una sola excepción para debilitarla.
teaching.explanationEs: Firm describe el tono; una sweeping statement (con everybody, nobody, always) es un punto débil de un texto.
segments: A sweeping statement such as everybody hates cycling may sound
firm, but a single exception is enough to undermine it.
teaching.audioText: A sweeping statement such as everybody hates cycling may sound firm, but a single exception is enough to undermine it.

teaching.en: Writers who deserve our trust back up their claims with evidence, whereas those who only want to persuade us often rely on emotion.
teaching.es: Los autores que merecen nuestra confianza respaldan sus afirmaciones con pruebas, mientras que los que solo quieren convencernos suelen apoyarse en la emoción.
teaching.explanationEs: Back up = respaldar con pruebas; persuade = convencer, a menudo con emoción además de datos.
segments: Writers who deserve our trust back up their claims with evidence, whereas
those who only want to persuade us often rely on emotion.
teaching.audioText: Writers who deserve our trust back up their claims with evidence, whereas those who only want to persuade us often rely on emotion.

prompt.es: Lee el texto y elige cuál es la tesis de la autora.

choices.text: Museums should charge no entrance fee, because fees keep out those who benefit most.
Museums should stay free only for children, because adults can afford the price.
Museums should raise their entrance fee, because galleries are short of money.

feedback.es: La tesis aparece tras «I will argue that»: una entrada de pago deja fuera a quienes más ganarían con la visita. Las otras opciones cambian el alcance o recogen la postura de los críticos.

hint.es: La tesis suele anunciarse con una fórmula como «I will argue that».

origin.text: Museums should be free for everyone. I will argue that an entrance fee quietly shuts out the very people who would benefit most from a visit. Critics claim that free entry would leave galleries short of money, and I concede that point: somebody has to pay for the roof. Nevertheless, when the capital opened its main museum without charge, visits doubled within a year, and donations rose as well. Surely a country that is proud of its past should let every child see it? Free entry may not solve every problem, but the evidence suggests that it is a sound choice, and it deserves the council's attention.

prompt.es: Elige qué función cumple esta pregunta dentro del texto.

choices.text: It genuinely asks readers to decide whether the evidence is convincing.
It presents the writer's view as obvious, inviting the reader to agree.
It admits that the evidence for the writer's claim is very weak.

feedback.es: Es una pregunta retórica: no espera respuesta ni pide al lector que valore las pruebas; da por obvia la tesis y empuja al lector a coincidir con ella.

hint.es: Fíjate en que nadie necesita contestar la pregunta: la respuesta ya está dada.

origin.text: Surely a country that is proud of its past should let every child see it?

prompt.es: Completa: «Los resultados podrían animar a otros municipios a probar la idea.»

feedback.es: Might, may o could suavizan la predicción: la autora admite que los datos de una sola ciudad no permiten asegurar el efecto.

hint.es: Es un verbo modal que expresa posibilidad, no certeza.

origin.text: The figures come from one city only. The results ___ encourage other councils to try the idea, but more data would help.

prompt.es: Según el texto, ¿qué prueba usa la autora para respaldar su tesis?

choices.text: Donations to the capital's main museum doubled once the charge was dropped.
Most parents in the capital said they would visit more often.
Visits to the capital's main museum doubled once the charge was dropped.

feedback.es: La prueba es un dato concreto de la capital: las visitas se duplicaron en un año sin entrada. Las donaciones solo subieron (no se duplicaron) y no hay encuesta a padres.

origin.text: Museums should be free for everyone. I will argue that an entrance fee quietly shuts out the very people who would benefit most from a visit. Critics claim that free entry would leave galleries short of money, and I concede that point: somebody has to pay for the roof. Nevertheless, when the capital opened its main museum without charge, visits doubled within a year, and donations rose as well. Surely a country that is proud of its past should let every child see it? Free entry may not solve every problem, but the evidence suggests that it is a sound choice, and it deserves the council's attention.

prompt.es: Escucha el comentario y elige qué tono predomina.

choices.text: Personal and firm, though ready to accept that the cost is real.
Bitter and sarcastic, convinced that councils will never take the problem seriously.
Detached and analytical, weighing the cost of the scheme without sharing any personal story.

feedback.es: El hablante cuenta una experiencia propia (la furgoneta), defiende su idea con firmeza y reconoce que el costo es real: firme pero dispuesto a conceder, ni amargo ni distante.

origin.audio: I have cycled to work for twelve years, and I can tell you that paint is not safety. Last spring a van clipped me in a lane that the council proudly called safe. I am not saying that every road needs a concrete wall, and I accept that the cost is real. But surely a child on a bicycle deserves more than a white line? If councils want more people to cycle, they must first make it feel safe.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase con el recurso que usa el autor.

pairs: Admittedly, the scheme is not cheap.
Visits doubled in the first year alone.
It would seem that the trial has worked.
Surely no one wants to see it close?

feedback.es: Admittedly reconoce un punto contrario, la cifra es una prueba, it would seem limita la afirmación y surely…? da la respuesta por obvia.

pairs: Admittedly, the scheme is not cheap.
Visits doubled in the first year alone.
It would seem that the trial has worked.
Surely no one wants to see it close?

prompt.es: ¿Qué postura adopta el autor ante quienes critican el trabajo remoto?

choices.text: He rejects their worry out of hand and argues that offices no longer matter at all.
He takes their worry seriously but thinks it is a poor reason for a fixed rule.
He shares their worry but believes that the evidence is still too weak to decide.

feedback.es: Admite que algunos empleados pueden rendir menos, pero concluye que eso no justifica imponer cinco días de oficina: toma en serio la objeción sin aceptarla como regla.

origin.text: Remote work is not the threat that some managers imagine. Critics argue that employees who stay at home are less productive, and I admit that a few may well be. Yet the largest study on the subject, covering some ten thousand workers, found that work stayed just as good, while far fewer people quit their jobs. Surely a firm that cares about results should welcome that? I am not saying that the office is useless; teams probably benefit from meeting regularly. Even so, insisting on five days a week seems to me a habit rather than a strategy, and it may cost companies their best people.

prompt.es: ¿Con qué propósito escribe «I am not saying that the office is useless»?

choices.text: To step back from his thesis and accept that offices are still necessary.
To reassure managers that employees will still work well from home.
To deal with an objection early and keep his argument fair.

feedback.es: Se adelanta a una objeción («entonces, ¿la oficina no sirve?») y limita su tesis para que siga siendo creíble; no retrocede en ella ni busca tranquilizar a los jefes sobre el rendimiento.

origin.text: Remote work is not the threat that some managers imagine. Critics argue that employees who stay at home are less productive, and I admit that a few may well be. Yet the largest study on the subject, covering some ten thousand workers, found that work stayed just as good, while far fewer people quit their jobs. Surely a firm that cares about results should welcome that? I am not saying that the office is useless; teams probably benefit from meeting regularly. Even so, insisting on five days a week seems to me a habit rather than a strategy, and it may cost companies their best people.

prompt.es: Escucha el fragmento de la reunión: ¿qué da a entender la directora?

choices.text: She is ready to approve the proposal, but only after a smaller trial.
She likes the detail but thinks another team should run the project.
She backs the proposal fully and considers the timeline perfectly realistic.

feedback.es: Elogia la propuesta, duda del calendario y propone un piloto más pequeño: apoya la idea con condiciones; no pide que otro equipo la dirija ni la aprueba sin reservas.

origin.audio: I have read the proposal twice, and I have to say that it is detailed. However, I cannot help wondering whether the timeline is realistic, given that the team is already stretched. I would be happy to support it, provided we agree a few conditions first. Perhaps we could start with a smaller pilot and review the results in the spring?

prompt.es: Completa: «La autora concede un punto, pero insiste en que no hacer nada costaría más.»

feedback.es: Concede a point es la colocación para reconocer que los críticos tienen parte de razón antes de defender la propia tesis.

origin.text: Critics say that the scheme is too expensive. The writer is happy to ___ a point, but she insists that doing nothing would cost more.

prompt.es: Elige la descripción más exacta del tono del autor.

choices.text: Bitter and angry, blaming the council for ignoring residents.
Disappointed but measured, acknowledging the council's difficulty.
Resigned and cold, accepting the cuts as necessary.

feedback.es: Se declara decepcionado, pero reconoce la presión del municipio (I do see the pressure) y pide una alternativa: tono mesurado, no rencoroso ni indiferente.

origin.text: The new bus timetable starts next week. To be honest, I am disappointed: buses will run half as often, although the town is growing. The council says that savings were necessary, and I do see the pressure it is under. Still, fewer buses will leave older residents stranded at home. Surely there is a fairer way to balance the books?

prompt.es: Escucha y elige cómo sostiene su tesis la hablante.

choices.text: Teenagers already eat well, so cooking lessons would add very little.
Cooking matters, but schools should wait until proper kitchens have been built.
Cooking deserves a place in the timetable, despite the cost involved.

feedback.es: Acepta que el horario está lleno y que las cocinas son caras, pero mantiene que cocinar es una habilidad vital: defiende la tesis reconociendo el costo.

origin.audio: In my opinion, every school should teach cooking. I know that timetables are already crowded, and I accept that kitchens are expensive to build. Yet cooking is a life skill, and it may well improve how teenagers eat. Why would we leave something so important to chance?

prompt.es: Completa: «Los autores matizan con prudencia sus resultados.»

feedback.es: Hedge es suavizar una afirmación con expresiones de cautela (suggests, appears) cuando no hay pruebas definitivas.

origin.text: Nobody can be certain yet. The authors carefully ___ their findings with words like suggests and appears, instead of claiming proof.

title.es: Proyecto de escritura: borrador y edición

es: Editar un borrador corrigiendo formas, registro y conectores (although, however, therefore, whereas), evitar el comma splice y justificar los cambios.

vocabulary.es: revisar una última vez, corregir pruebas
coma que une dos oraciones completas

teaching.en: I always leave a draft for a day before I edit it, because mistakes are much easier to spot with fresh eyes.
teaching.es: Siempre dejo un borrador un día antes de corregirlo, porque los errores se ven mucho mejor con ojos frescos.
teaching.explanationEs: Draft y edit: primero escribes una versión y luego la editas por pasadas: formas, registro y conectores.
segments: I always leave a draft for a day before I edit
it, because mistakes are much easier to spot with fresh eyes.
teaching.audioText: I always leave a draft for a day before I edit it, because mistakes are much easier to spot with fresh eyes.

teaching.en: Although the first version was clear, it was full of slang, so I had to tone down the language before sending it to the client.
teaching.es: Aunque la primera versión era clara, estaba llena de jerga, así que tuve que suavizar el lenguaje antes de enviarla al cliente.
teaching.explanationEs: Although + oración, oración: no lleva but. Tone down es suavizar un tono demasiado directo o coloquial.
segments: Although the first version was clear, it was full of slang, so I
had to tone down the language before sending it to the client.
teaching.audioText: Although the first version was clear, it was full of slang, so I had to tone down the language before sending it to the client.

teaching.en: The trial succeeded; however, the sample was small, and my first draft, with a comma instead of a semicolon before however, was a comma splice.
teaching.es: La prueba tuvo éxito; sin embargo, la muestra era pequeña, y mi primer borrador, con una coma en lugar de un punto y coma antes de however, era un comma splice.
teaching.explanationEs: However une dos oraciones: punto y coma antes y coma después. Con una coma sola se produce un comma splice.
segments: The trial succeeded; however, the sample was small, and my first draft, with
a comma instead of a semicolon before however, was a comma splice.
teaching.audioText: The trial succeeded; however, the sample was small, and my first draft, with a comma instead of a semicolon before however, was a comma splice.

teaching.en: Fuel prices rose sharply; therefore, many households cut back, whereas wealthier families barely noticed the difference.
teaching.es: Los precios del combustible subieron bruscamente; por lo tanto, muchos hogares gastaron menos, mientras que las familias más ricas casi no notaron la diferencia.
teaching.explanationEs: Therefore introduce la consecuencia con la misma puntuación que however; whereas contrasta dos grupos dentro de una oración.
segments: Fuel prices rose sharply; therefore, many households cut
back, whereas wealthier families barely noticed the difference.
teaching.audioText: Fuel prices rose sharply; therefore, many households cut back, whereas wealthier families barely noticed the difference.

teaching.en: A casual message to a colleague sounds friendly, but the same wording may seem careless in a report, so reword it carefully.
teaching.es: Un mensaje informal a un colega suena amistoso, pero las mismas palabras pueden parecer descuidadas en un informe, así que reformúlalo con cuidado.
teaching.explanationEs: Casual describe el registro informal; reword es decir lo mismo con otras palabras, más adecuadas al lector.
segments: A casual message to a colleague sounds friendly, but the same
wording may seem careless in a report, so reword it carefully.
teaching.audioText: A casual message to a colleague sounds friendly, but the same wording may seem careless in a report, so reword it carefully.

teaching.en: When you proofread your final draft, look for every sentence fragment, because a group of words without a main verb often passes for a full sentence.
teaching.es: Cuando revises tu borrador final, busca cada fragmento de oración, porque un grupo de palabras sin verbo principal suele parecer una oración completa a simple vista.
teaching.explanationEs: Proofread es la última lectura, centrada en errores pequeños; un sentence fragment es un trozo de frase que se presenta como si fuera una oración.
segments: When you proofread your final draft, look for every sentence fragment, because a
group of words without a main verb often passes for a full sentence.
teaching.audioText: When you proofread your final draft, look for every sentence fragment, because a group of words without a main verb often passes for a full sentence.

prompt.es: Elige la corrección de «Although the lanes are cheap, but they are narrow».

choices.text: Although the lanes are cheap, however, they are narrow.
Although the lanes are cheap, they are narrow.
Although the lanes are cheap; they are narrow.

feedback.es: Although ya expresa el contraste: la segunda parte no lleva but ni however, y tampoco va separada con punto y coma.

hint.es: Con although no se necesita otro conector en la segunda parte.

origin.text: Draft report: The new cycling scheme is a total mess. Although the lanes are cheap, but they are narrow; however the council built them anyway. The kids who ride to school hate them, therefore fewer of them are cycling. Some parents like the lanes, whereas others is worried about the traffic. Honestly, the whole plan is a bit rubbish and needs fixing fast.

prompt.es: Completa: «La muestra era pequeña; sin embargo, los autores siguen cautos.»

feedback.es: However (o nevertheless) une dos oraciones con contraste: punto y coma antes y coma después.

hint.es: Es el conector de contraste que aparece entre dos oraciones completas.

origin.text: The trial was a success. The sample was small; ___, the authors remain cautious.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Muchos hogares gastaron menos, mientras que otros casi no lo notaron.»

answer.text: Many households cut back whereas others barely noticed the difference
accepted: Many households cut back whereas others barely noticed the difference
Whereas many households cut back others barely noticed the difference

feedback.es: Whereas contrasta los dos grupos dentro de la misma oración, sin punto y coma.

hint.es: Whereas une las dos partes sin punto y coma.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada conector con la función que cumple en la frase.

pairs: Although the plan is cheap, it is slow.

pairs.es: concesión al inicio de la frase

pairs: The plan is cheap; however, it is slow.
Prices rose; therefore, sales fell.
Some like the plan, whereas others oppose it.

feedback.es: Although concede al inicio, however contrasta entre oraciones, therefore presenta el resultado y whereas opone dos grupos.

pairs: Although the plan is cheap, it is slow.

pairs.es: concesión al inicio de la frase

pairs: The plan is cheap; however, it is slow.
Prices rose; therefore, sales fell.
Some like the plan, whereas others oppose it.

prompt.es: Elige la versión formal y bien puntuada de la frase del borrador.

choices.text: The kids who cycle to school dislike the lanes; therefore fewer of them cycle.
The children who cycle to school hate the lanes, therefore, fewer of them cycle.
The children who cycle to school dislike the lanes; therefore, fewer of them cycle.

feedback.es: Children y dislike elevan el registro, y therefore entre dos oraciones lleva punto y coma antes y coma después.

origin.text: Draft report: The new cycling scheme is a total mess. Although the lanes are cheap, but they are narrow; however the council built them anyway. The kids who ride to school hate them, therefore fewer of them are cycling. Some parents like the lanes, whereas others is worried about the traffic. Honestly, the whole plan is a bit rubbish and needs fixing fast.

prompt.es: Completa el informe con el conector adecuado en cada espacio.

feedback.es: Therefore introduce la consecuencia del éxito del piloto y although concede que los datos son alentadores sin cerrar el tema.

sentences: The pilot scheme was a success; ___, several councils have copied it.
___ the evidence is encouraging, more data would help.

prompt.es: ¿Qué da a entender la tutora sobre el borrador?

choices.text: That its content is sound, but its register is too casual for a board.
That its content is sound, but it is too long for a board to read.
That its register is right, but its evidence needs to be better organised.

feedback.es: Elogia el argumento y las pruebas, pero dice que suena a mensaje a un amigo: el contenido es bueno y falla el registro; no habla de la extensión ni de la organización de las pruebas.

origin.text: Tutor's comment on a student essay: The argument is sound, and the evidence is well chosen. Even so, the piece reads more like a message to a friend than a report for the board; a little more care with register would go a long way.

prompt.es: Completa: «Por favor, suaviza el lenguaje antes de que enviemos el segundo correo.»

feedback.es: Tone down es el verbo frasal para suavizar un tono demasiado directo antes de enviar el mensaje.

origin.text: The client found our first email too direct. Please ___ down the language before we send the second one.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Aunque el informe es breve, contiene pruebas sólidas.»

answer.text: Although the report is short it contains strong evidence
accepted: Although the report is short it contains strong evidence
It contains strong evidence although the report is short

feedback.es: Although abre la concesión y no admite but en la segunda parte: la frase sigue con it contains.

prompt.es: Corrige el borrador (seis errores) y justifica dos cambios con «because».

answer.text: Dear Ms Clark, the children in my class were very excited about the trip. Although the tickets were expensive, we are going to go anyway. The museum is free; however, it closes early; therefore, we must leave at two. I changed kids to children because a formal letter needs a neutral register, and I removed but because although already shows the contrast.
accepted: Dear Ms Clark, the children in my class were very excited about the trip. Although the tickets were expensive, we are going to go anyway. The museum is free; however, it closes early; therefore, we must leave at two. I changed kids to children because a formal letter needs a neutral register, and I removed but because although already shows the contrast.

Dear Ms Clark, the pupils in my class were very excited about the trip. Although the tickets were costly, we are going to go anyway. The museum is free; nevertheless, it closes early; as a result, we must leave at two. I replaced kids with pupils because a formal letter needs a neutral register, and I deleted but because although already shows the contrast.

feedback.es: Un buen borrador editado usa children, were y going to; corrige although sin but; puntúa however y therefore con punto y coma y coma, y explica dos cambios con because.

origin.text: Borrador: «Dear Ms Clark, the kids in my class was very excited about the trip. Although the tickets were pricey, but we are gonna go anyway. The museum is free, however it closes early, therefore we must leave at two.» Reescríbelo en un registro formal, corrige la concordancia y los conectores y añade dos frases que justifiquen dos cambios (empieza con I changed… o I removed…).

prompt.es: ¿Con qué propósito cambia el editor «kids» y «gonna»?

choices.text: To correct two errors of form that would have confused the board.
To stop the informal wording from distracting the board from strong findings.
To make the report sound more confident about its findings.

feedback.es: El editor lo aclara: los hallazgos son fuertes y no quiere que una frase informal distraiga; es un cambio de registro, no de gramática ni de tono de seguridad.

origin.text: Editor's note: I have replaced kids with children and gonna with going to. The findings are strong, and I do not want a casual phrase to distract the board from them.

prompt.es: Completa: «Antes de enviarlo, revisa con cuidado tu informe final.»

feedback.es: Proofread es la última lectura, centrada en errores pequeños, antes de entregar el texto final.

origin.text: You have finished the final draft of your report. Before you send it, please ___ it carefully, because one small mistake can spoil a good report.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Los resultados fueron alentadores; sin embargo, la muestra era pequeña.»

answer.text: The results were encouraging however the sample was small
accepted: The results were encouraging however the sample was small
The results were encouraging the sample however was small

feedback.es: However une las dos oraciones con contraste: los resultados son buenos y la muestra limita la conclusión.

es: Combinar la información de un audio y de un texto sobre un mismo tema, atribuir cada dato a su fuente y señalar coincidencias, diferencias y discrepancias.

vocabulary.es: en desacuerdo con, en contradicción con

teaching.en: According to the voicemail, the pool will reopen on Thursday, but the notice on the door gives a different day.
teaching.es: Según el mensaje de voz, la piscina reabrirá el jueves, pero el aviso de la puerta indica otro día.
teaching.explanationEs: According to + fuente atribuye el dato a quien lo dice; no se usa con uno mismo.
segments: According to the voicemail, the pool will reopen on Thursday,
but the notice on the door gives a different day.
teaching.audioText: According to the voicemail, the pool will reopen on Thursday, but the notice on the door gives a different day.

teaching.en: When two sources differ from each other on a key detail such as the opening time, a careful reader reports the discrepancy instead of quietly choosing one version.
teaching.es: Cuando dos fuentes difieren entre sí en un dato clave, como la hora de apertura, un lector cuidadoso señala la discrepancia en lugar de elegir una versión sin decir nada.
teaching.explanationEs: Differ from: las fuentes no coinciden. Discrepancy es el nombre de esa diferencia entre datos que deberían ser iguales.
segments: When two sources differ from each other on a key detail such as the
opening time, a careful reader reports the discrepancy instead of quietly choosing one version.
teaching.audioText: When two sources differ from each other on a key detail such as the opening time, a careful reader reports the discrepancy instead of quietly choosing one version.

teaching.en: A second account can corroborate a figure, so a detail confirmed twice is more trustworthy than one mentioned only once.
teaching.es: Un segundo relato puede corroborar una cifra, así que un dato confirmado dos veces es más fiable que uno mencionado una sola vez.
teaching.explanationEs: Corroborate: confirmar un dato con otra fuente independiente; aumenta su fiabilidad.
segments: A second account can corroborate a figure, so a detail
confirmed twice is more trustworthy than one mentioned only once.
teaching.audioText: A second account can corroborate a figure, so a detail confirmed twice is more trustworthy than one mentioned only once.

teaching.en: Both the voicemail and the notice promise a lifeguard on every shift, but only the notice says that young children must come with an adult.
teaching.es: Tanto el mensaje de voz como el aviso prometen un socorrista en cada turno, pero solo el aviso dice que los niños pequeños deben venir con un adulto.
teaching.explanationEs: Both + plural marca lo que coincide; only the notice señala un detalle que aporta una sola fuente.
segments: Both the voicemail and the notice promise a lifeguard on every shift, but

prompt.es: Escribe tu intervención de un minuto: postura, concesión y cautela.

answer.text: I firmly believe that public transport in our city should be free for everyone. First, it would help families who spend a large part of their income on travel, and it would encourage more people to leave their cars at home. As a result, the streets would be quieter, the air would be cleaner and the centre would be safer for children. It is true that free buses would cost the council a great deal of money, and some critics argue that the service might become crowded. To some extent, I share that worry. However, it seems that the money could come from parking fees and from the money that we already spend on roads. Perhaps we could begin with a one-year trial and review the results carefully. On the other hand, nobody can promise that every passenger would leave a car at home. Even so, on balance, I would say that the benefits outweigh the costs, and I stand by that view. In short, free public transport would make our city fairer, cleaner and calmer.
accepted: I firmly believe that public transport in our city should be free for everyone. First, it would help families who spend a large part of their income on travel, and it would encourage more people to leave their cars at home. As a result, the streets would be quieter, the air would be cleaner and the centre would be safer for children. It is true that free buses would cost the council a great deal of money, and some critics argue that the service might become crowded. To some extent, I share that worry. However, it seems that the money could come from parking fees and from the money that we already spend on roads. Perhaps we could begin with a one-year trial and review the results carefully. On the other hand, nobody can promise that every passenger would leave a car at home. Even so, on balance, I would say that the benefits outweigh the costs, and I stand by that view. In short, free public transport would make our city fairer, cleaner and calmer.

My position is clear: public transport should cost nothing for residents. Admittedly, it is not a cheap idea, and the council would have to find a large sum every year. Even so, I am convinced that the money would be well spent. Cheaper travel would help students, workers and older people who cannot afford a car, and it may also reduce traffic in the centre. Some say that buses would become crowded, and I agree that the service would need more vehicles. Perhaps the city could add a few routes at busy hours and review the plan after twelve months. It seems to me that nobody can be certain of the result before trying. However, doing nothing is also a choice, and it has costs of its own: noise, pollution and long delays. To sum up, free transport is a fair and sensible idea, and on balance I think it is worth a try.

teaching.audioText: To hold your ground without sounding rude, acknowledge the other person's concern first and only then state your position clearly.

teaching.en: Writing with tact means you strike a balance between honesty and courtesy, and a little nuance shows that you have weighed both sides.
teaching.es: Escribir con tacto significa encontrar un equilibrio entre la sinceridad y la cortesía, y un poco de matiz demuestra que has sopesado ambas partes.
teaching.explanationEs: Strike a balance: encontrar el punto medio; nuance es la mezcla de concesión, cautela y firmeza.
segments: Writing with tact means you strike a balance between honesty and courtesy,
and a little nuance shows that you have weighed both sides.
teaching.audioText: Writing with tact means you strike a balance between honesty and courtesy, and a little nuance shows that you have weighed both sides.

prompt.es: Interpreta el mensaje: ¿qué da a entender el compañero?

choices.text: He sincerely believes that everybody has been too busy, and sees no problem.
He politely implies that somebody forgot to update the calendar.
He is asking colleagues to empty the calendar so that it can be updated.

feedback.es: No acusa a nadie, pero «left blank again» y «I am sure everybody has had a lot on» sugieren con cortesía que alguien olvidó rellenarlo; tomarlo al pie de la letra sería no leer entre líneas.

hint.es: Fíjate en lo que dice sobre el calendario sin pedirlo directamente.

origin.text: Note from a colleague: I see that the shared calendar has been left blank again this week. I am sure that everybody has had a lot on.

prompt.es: Completa: «Nunca dice que está molesta, pero hay que leer entre líneas.»

feedback.es: Read between the lines es captar lo que un mensaje sugiere sin decirlo de forma explícita.

hint.es: La preposición significa «entre» y aparece en la enseñanza.

origin.text: Your manager's email never says that she is unhappy with you, but you have to read ___ the lines.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Gracias por la oferta; sin embargo, debo rechazarla.»

answer.text: Thank you for the offer nevertheless I must decline it

feedback.es: Se agradece primero, y nevertheless introduce el rechazo con decline: cortés pero claro.

hint.es: Empieza agradeciendo y deja nevertheless para el rechazo.

prompt.es: Escucha el mensaje: ¿qué quiere decir en realidad Elena?

choices.text: She is sincerely reassuring him that the bins were not a problem at all.
She is warning him that the council will fine everyone for blocked pavements.
She is politely complaining and hopes it will not happen again.

feedback.es: Elena suaviza la queja («I am sure it was just a mistake») pero deja claro que los contenedores bloquearon la acera: es una queja cortés, no una tranquilización.

origin.audio: Hi, it is Elena from upstairs. I hope you do not mind me mentioning this, but I could not help noticing that the recycling bins were still on the pavement on Friday morning. I am sure it was just a mistake, and I know how busy this month has been for everybody. It is only that the pavement was blocked for a while. Anyway, thanks so much, and I hope you have a lovely weekend.

prompt.es: Elige la respuesta que agradece, reconoce sus costos y defiende tu postura.

choices.text: Thank you for explaining. I understand your costs; nevertheless, could we discuss a smaller rise?
Thank you for explaining. I understand your costs, so I accept the rise without any question.
Thank you for explaining, but the rise is unfair, and I expect you to cancel it.

feedback.es: Agradece, reconoce el problema del casero y propone hablar: es cortés y defiende su postura; una respuesta cede sin más y la otra exige sin matiz.

origin.text: Your landlord writes: From next month the rent will rise, as our costs have gone up. I trust that this will not be a problem.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase con su función en la respuesta final.

pairs: Thank you for letting me know.
I am afraid I must decline.
On balance, I think the plan is fair.
Could we agree to meet on Friday?

feedback.es: Thank you reconoce, I am afraid I must decline rechaza con suavidad, on balance matiza la postura y Could we agree…? propone un acuerdo.

prompt.es: ¿Qué espera realmente Helen de Tom?

choices.text: That he leaves the report as it is, because it was already detailed.
That he revises the cost section before the board meets on Thursday.
That he postpones sending the report until after the board meeting.

feedback.es: «I did wonder whether the section on costs might benefit from more explanation» es una petición cortés: quiere que lo revise antes del jueves.

origin.text: Dear Tom, thank you for your report, which was, as always, detailed. I did wonder whether the section on costs might benefit from a little more explanation, and perhaps a second pair of eyes before it goes to the board on Thursday. No rush, of course. Kind regards, Helen.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué postura defiende la hablante.

choices.text: She rejects the plan completely and proposes a smaller scheme.
She is unsure about the plan and asks for another proposal.
She defends the plan while admitting that it has some flaws.

feedback.es: Admite que el plan no es perfecto, pero mantiene con firmeza que es la opción más justa: postura defendida con matiz.

origin.audio: I admit that the plan is not perfect, and I can see why some residents are anxious. Even so, I firmly believe that it is the fairest option we have. A smaller scheme would hardly make a difference, whereas doing nothing would cost us far more in the long run.

prompt.es: Completa: «No quiero ser grosero, pero debo discrepar de las cifras de tu informe.»

feedback.es: Take issue with es la colocación para discrepar de algo con educación pero con claridad.

origin.text: I do not want to sound rude, but I must ___ issue with the figures in your report.

prompt.es: Responde al mensaje con tacto y defiende tu postura con matiz.

answer.text: Hi Sam, thank you for your message. I think you are saying that the cleaning is not shared fairly, and I understand why you feel that way. It is true that I have been out a lot this month, and I admit that some weeks you have done more than your part. However, I firmly believe that the problem is partly my work schedule, because I finish late on most days and I am often too tired to clean. To some extent, that may explain why the flat looks worse than before. I am afraid I cannot clean every day, but I would like to find a fair solution. I also want to say that I appreciate how much you have done, and I do not want this to become a bigger problem between us. Could we agree to make a weekly calendar? I could take the kitchen on Saturdays, and you could choose another task. What do you think? Let us review the plan in two weeks. Thanks again for being honest with me.
accepted: Hi Sam, thank you for your message. I think you are saying that the cleaning is not shared fairly, and I understand why you feel that way. It is true that I have been out a lot this month, and I admit that some weeks you have done more than your part. However, I firmly believe that the problem is partly my work schedule, because I finish late on most days and I am often too tired to clean. To some extent, that may explain why the flat looks worse than before. I am afraid I cannot clean every day, but I would like to find a fair solution. I also want to say that I appreciate how much you have done, and I do not want this to become a bigger problem between us. Could we agree to make a weekly calendar? I could take the kitchen on Saturdays, and you could choose another task. What do you think? Let us review the plan in two weeks. Thanks again for being honest with me.

Hello Sam, thanks for telling me how you feel. Your message suggests that I am not doing enough, and I can see why you are upset. Admittedly, I have not cleaned much lately, and I am sorry about that. Still, my new job means that I work late most evenings, so perhaps the real problem is time, not effort. I am not sure that a strict rule would help, but a simple calendar might. What if we share the tasks by day, and I take the bathroom and the kitchen at weekends? We could try it for a month and then check whether it works for both of us. I would also like us to be more open with each other, because small problems grow when nobody talks about them. I hope that sounds fair, and thank you for being patient with me. Let us talk about it over dinner this week, and then we can write the calendar together.

feedback.es: Una buena respuesta interpreta lo implícito, agradece, concede un punto, defiende la postura con cautela y propone un plan concreto.

origin.text: Caso final. Tu compañero de casa escribe: «Some of us seem to do all the cleaning while others are always out.» Escribe entre 160 y 270 palabras: interpreta lo que implica, agradece, reconoce un punto, defiende tu postura con cautela (tu horario de trabajo te deja poco tiempo) y propón un plan (un calendario) con un acuerdo concreto.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Entiendo tu preocupación; sin embargo, mantengo mi postura.»

answer.text: I understand your concern nevertheless I keep my position

feedback.es: Se reconoce primero la preocupación y nevertheless marca el contraste: se mantiene la postura sin romper la cortesía.

prompt.es: Elige la respuesta con más tacto y matiz a la propuesta.

choices.text: Thank you for the idea. I admit it helps some people, but eight is hard for parents.
I take issue with this plan. Eight is far too early, and I am sure that everybody agrees with me.
Thanks, eight is fine. I will tell the others, even though I think that it is quite unfair.

feedback.es: Agradece, admite un punto a favor y expone el problema con matiz; las otras respuestas confrontan o ceden en contra de su opinión.

origin.text: Your manager proposes moving the weekly meeting to eight in the morning. Several colleagues have small children, and you think the plan is unfair, but you want to stay on good terms.

prompt.es: Escucha el mensaje y elige cómo suena la hablante.

choices.text: Enthusiastic: she is pleased to have one more meeting this week.
Sarcastic: she is unhappy about the plan and says the opposite.
Neutral: she is reporting the new time without any opinion about it.

feedback.es: «Oh, brilliant… Just what we needed» es sarcasmo: dice lo contrario de lo que siente, porque no quiere otra reunión a las ocho; no es entusiasmo ni un aviso neutral.

origin.audio: Oh, brilliant. Another meeting at eight in the morning. Just what we needed after the week we have had. I am sure everybody will be thrilled to give up their Friday evening too.
